Kaladin speaks the Fourth Ideal, accepting that he cannot protect everyone, and comes into greater power, but his former friend Moash murders the beloved bridgeman Teft, a loss that guts him even in victory. In the spren realm Adolin's trial wins a measure of alliance and revives his once-dead sword, and Shallan resolves more of her hidden past and the secret society hunting her. Venli leads a group of her people toward freedom. Then the war turns on a single stroke: as the god of hatred moves to cast aside the dying King Taravangian, Taravangian instead outmaneuvers and kills him, seizing the divine power and becoming a new, far more cunning god of hatred. With a contest of champions set to decide the war on a fixed near-future date, the coalition faces an enemy deadlier than the one it thought it was fighting.

characters.description: The youngest of the Ingleside children, not quite fifteen when the book opens, pretty, vain of her looks, and the only Blythe with no ambition beyond a few years of parties and good times before she settles down. She is sensitive about the slight lisp that comes back when she is agitated, hates responsibility, and has never been asked to be useful in her life. Her elder brothers and sisters are grown and mostly away at college; she is still a schoolgirl at home with her mother and Susan.
characters.name: Rilla Blythe

characters.description: Mistress of Ingleside, with a grown family scattered between home and college. She is happy, settled, and, at the opening of the book, chiefly occupied with her children's futures and the ordinary business of the Glen.
characters.name: Anne Blythe

characters.description: The doctor at Glen St. Mary, long established in his practice, and the steady centre of the Ingleside household.
characters.name: Gilbert Blythe

characters.description: The Ingleside housekeeper of many years, elderly now, fiercely devoted to the family, and the household's most reliable source of opinion. She reads the newspaper aloud, argues with the world, and refuses on principle to be discouraged by anything.
characters.name: Susan Baker

characters.description: Once Miss Cornelia Bryant of Four Winds, now Mrs. Marshall Elliott of the Glen, still blunt and still practical, and a constant visitor at the Ingleside kitchen with the news of the district.
characters.name: Mrs. Marshall Elliott

characters.description: The eldest Blythe son, just finished at Redmond and about to begin medicine, red-haired, energetic, and impatient for something worth doing. He is quietly attached to Faith Meredith and owns a small brown-and-white dog who will not leave his side.
characters.name: Jem Blythe

characters.description: The second Blythe son, home from Redmond after an illness, beautiful, dreamy, and a poet. He loves the valley, hates ugliness and cruelty more than most people can understand, and has always been closer to Rilla than any of the others. Years ago he told the children that he had seen the Pied Piper coming over the hills.
characters.name: Walter Blythe

characters.description: The quiet Blythe son, brown and self-contained, still a schoolboy at the opening of the book and Susan's particular charge since his difficult infancy. He says little and thinks a good deal.
characters.name: Shirley Blythe

characters.description: A schoolteacher who boards at Ingleside, some fifteen years older than Rilla and her closest confidante. Dark, clever, and given to moods, she is engaged to a man working abroad and is troubled by vivid dreams she believes to be prophetic.
characters.name: Gertrude Oliver

characters.description: The son of Owen and Leslie Ford of the little house on Four Winds Harbour, a visitor to the Glen in the summers, older than Rilla and much admired by every girl in the district. Easy, teasing, and well travelled, he takes notice of Rilla at her first grown-up party.
characters.name: Kenneth Ford

characters.description: The eldest of the manse children, now grown, a beautiful and warm-hearted young woman studying at Redmond, still as fearless and impulsive as she was as a child, and long understood to belong to Jem Blythe.
characters.name: Faith Meredith

characters.description: The quieter Meredith daughter, gentle, watchful, and reserved, who keeps house at the manse and keeps her own feelings entirely to herself.
characters.name: Una Meredith

characters.description: Brought up by Mrs. Marshall Elliott since she was found as a runaway child, and now a young woman of the Glen, still plain-spoken to the point of rudeness, engaged to a local man and full of the district's news.
characters.name: Mary Vance

characters.description: Jem Blythe's small, ugly, devoted dog, who follows him everywhere and is uneasy whenever his master is out of sight.
characters.name: Dog Monday

characters.description: A newborn baby whose mother has died and whose father has gone overseas, found by Rilla in a wretched house up the Glen and carried home in a soup tureen because there was nothing else to put him in. He is sickly, ugly, and entirely unwanted by anyone else.
characters.name: James Kitchener Anderson

characters.description: A prosperous, disagreeable Glen farmer with long whiskers, known throughout the district by an unflattering nickname, who holds and loudly airs opinions that set him against most of his neighbours.
characters.name: Mr. Pryor

characters.description: Mr. Pryor's daughter, a pale, timid, colourless girl of Rilla's acquaintance who has never in her life stood up to her father, and who is in love with a young man of the Glen.
characters.name: Miranda Pryor

characters.description: The small son of the minister and his second wife, a solemn, intense child who takes everything he is told with complete literalness and feels things far beyond his years.
characters.name: Bruce Meredith

recaps.ending: The war ends. Jem Blythe, missing for months, is found to have been a prisoner in Germany, escapes, and comes home lame but alive, and Dog Monday's long vigil at the station platform ends when he finally meets the right train. Jerry Meredith recovers from his wound and Carl Meredith comes home having lost an eye. Shirley returns from the flying corps. Susan Baker, having refused a proposal of marriage during the war, takes a modest holiday of her own at the end of it. Gertrude Oliver is married to her fiancé. Jims's father comes back from France, marries again, and takes the boy, so Rilla gives up the child she raised from a soup tureen and finds she has grown up in the process. Walter is not among the returning. His mother, his family, and Una Meredith, who never told anyone what she felt for him, carry that loss into the peace, and his last poem has made him known far beyond the Glen. Kenneth Ford comes back at last and walks up to Ingleside, and when he asks Rilla whether she has kept the promise she made him the night before he sailed, her old childhood lisp returns in her answer. Rilla ends the book engaged, and the Glen begins the long work of living afterwards.
recaps.in_short: Rilla Blythe is not quite fifteen and wants nothing but a few years of parties when the First World War begins on the night of her first grown-up dance. Over the next four years the war takes her brothers and her friends: Jem enlists at once, Jerry Meredith with him, and Walter, held back at first by illness and then tormented for not going, enlists in his turn. Rilla, who has never been useful in her life, brings home an orphaned newborn in a soup tureen and raises him, founds and runs a Junior Red Cross, and learns to wait and work while the casualty lists come in. Jem's dog takes up a station-platform vigil that lasts the whole war. Walter is killed at the front, and his last letter to Rilla asks her not to grieve. Later Jem is reported wounded and missing, and the family lives for months in uncertainty before learning that he is a prisoner and has escaped. The armistice comes; Jem, Shirley, Jerry, and Carl come home, Walter does not, and Rilla, grown up, is claimed by Kenneth Ford.

recaps.text: Previously: Anne Shirley, brought up as an orphan at Green Gables in Avonlea, married Doctor Gilbert Blythe and has raised their family at Ingleside in Glen St. Mary, with the housekeeper Susan Baker and the old friend once known as Miss Cornelia Bryant, now Mrs. Marshall Elliott, close at hand. The Blythe children are Jem, Walter, the twins Nan and Di, Shirley, and the youngest, Rilla. Their closest friends are the children of the Glen manse: Jerry, Faith, Una, and Carl Meredith, whose widowed father, the Reverend John Meredith, married Rosemary West after a long delay caused by a promise Rosemary had made to her sister. As children the two families spent their summers in a wooded hollow they called Rainbow Valley, where Walter once told them he had seen the Pied Piper coming over the hills and they promised to follow when he called. The elder children are now grown and mostly away at Redmond College. This book opens in the summer of 1914.

Rilla Blythe, the youngest at Ingleside and not yet fifteen, is looking forward to four carefree years before she need think about anything. The household gathers for the summer: Jem home from Redmond and quietly attached to Faith Meredith, Walter recovering from typhoid, Nan and Di, Shirley, and Gertrude Oliver, the schoolteacher who boards at Ingleside and is Rilla's confidante. Gertrude is uneasy over a dream she cannot explain. Rilla goes to her first grown-up party, a dance at the Four Winds lighthouse, wearing her first long dress, and is noticed by Kenneth Ford. In the middle of the evening word arrives that Britain has declared war on Germany, and the young men talk of nothing else. Rilla, whose slippers have been taken as a joke, walks home barefoot and humiliated, and afterwards remembers that night as the last of the old world.

Jem enlists in the first days, along with Jerry Meredith, and the Glen begins to divide between those who are going and those who are not. Walter, still weak from illness, cannot go, and takes his exclusion harder than anyone guesses. When Jem's train pulls out, his dog follows it to the station and refuses to come home, settling in the shed by the platform to watch every train that comes in, and there he stays. Sent up the Glen on an errand, Rilla finds a newborn baby in a wretched house where the mother has died and the father has gone overseas, and carries the child home in a soup tureen for want of anything else. Challenged by her mother to take the responsibility or give it up, she keeps him, names him Jims, and begins to learn from a book how to raise a baby. She also founds a Junior Red Cross among the Glen girls and finds herself its president.

The war settles into a long ordeal at home. Susan reads the despatches aloud and follows the fighting on a map; every reverse is argued over in the Ingleside kitchen and every list of casualties is read with dread. Jem writes from the front. Rilla struggles with Jims, who thrives despite her inexperience, and with the Junior Red Cross, which teaches her to organize, to endure disagreeable people, and to finish what she begins. The heavy Canadian losses in the spring fighting bring the war home to the Glen for the first time, and the district begins to count its own dead. Walter, well again, is bitterly conscious that he has not enlisted; he is talked about, and one day he receives an envelope containing a white feather. He says nothing about it to his family, and Rilla, who understands him better than anyone, watches him with growing fear.

Walter decides to enlist and tells Rilla first, out in the valley. He explains that he is going precisely because he is afraid, that he could not live with staying at home, and that he has no illusions about what he is going to. Anne bears it without protest, and Rilla promises him that she will not cry when he goes and will keep her courage while he is away. Walter trains, and then sails. Una Meredith says goodbye to him and keeps to herself what it costs her. Ingleside settles into the routine of waiting: letters, parcels, Red Cross work, and the newspaper. Rilla is no longer the girl who wanted only a good time; she runs her committee, raises Jims, and holds herself together in public. Kenneth Ford, before he goes overseas himself, comes to Ingleside to say goodbye and asks Rilla for a promise she keeps privately and takes entirely seriously.

Rilla takes on the affairs of a timid Glen girl whose father, who is against the war, has forbidden her to marry her soldier before he sails; Rilla arranges the wedding herself, in the man's own house, and carries it off. Life at home goes on in a mixture of small comedy and constant dread. Then, one night, Jem's dog howls at the station, and the household knows without being told that something has happened. Word follows that Walter has been killed in action in France. His last letter reaches Rilla afterwards: he tells her that he had known he would not come back, that he was not afraid at the end, and that she is not to grieve for him but to keep her courage. Rilla does not cry. The poem Walter wrote at the front is published and read across the country. Ingleside goes on, and Anne, after a long illness of grief, gets up again because the others need her.

The war drags into its worst years. Shirley turns eighteen and enlists in the flying corps, and his mother has to let another son go. Carl Meredith is at the front and Jerry Meredith is badly wounded. Susan Baker receives, and briskly refuses, a proposal of marriage from a neighbour she despises. The great German advance in the spring brings the Glen its blackest Sunday, when the news seems to leave no hope at all and only Susan refuses to admit defeat. Then Ingleside is told that Jem has been wounded and is missing, and there the matter rests: month after month passes with no word whether he is alive or dead, while his dog keeps his place at the station. Rilla, hardened and entirely grown up, keeps the household and her mother going. Faith Meredith, nursing overseas, waits as they all wait.

Word comes at last that Jem is alive, a prisoner in Germany. He escapes, and in time he comes home, lame and much altered but himself, and his dog's long watch on the station platform is over. The tide turns on the western front, and the armistice is celebrated in the Glen with bells and bonfires. Carl Meredith returns having lost an eye, Jerry recovers, and Shirley comes back from the flying corps. Susan takes a modest holiday of her own, and Gertrude Oliver is married. Jims's father comes home from France, marries again, and claims his son, so Rilla gives up the child she raised and understands how much the four years have made of her. Walter does not return, and his family and Una Meredith carry that with them into the peace. Kenneth Ford comes back at last and walks up to Ingleside, and when he asks Rilla whether she kept the promise she made him before he sailed, the lisp of her childhood comes back in her answer. The book ends with Rilla engaged and the Glen beginning again.

characters.description: An unusually advanced Tier 2 ascender training at Lenton's desert camp after helping uncover an illegal operation. Imperial attention now threatens his safety, while a Challenger deadline requires him to hunt far above his tier.
characters.name: Jiran

characters.description: Jiran's cousin and training partner at the desert camp. She has reached Molding 37 and practices with a spear while Jiran helps her apply small, controlled forces to her bones and repair the resulting injuries with mana.
characters.name: Niya

characters.description: Jiran's instructor and protector at the desert camp. He orders Jiran to avoid trouble while they await an imperial envoy, but admits that he cannot shield his pupil from the emperor. He does not condemn Jiran for killing the slavers whose actions endangered others.
characters.name: Lenton

characters.description: A noble mentor traveling with Jiran's party. He must return to Feylon instead of accompanying Jiran toward the capital, and Jiran believes his unexplained curse is responsible for the separation. Jiran is determined to search for a cure.
characters.name: Feylon Samris

characters.description: A star-like woman encountered during Jiran's interrupted Challenger reward process. She says his use of Revelation created her, calls Jiran her father, and depends on his mana to remain conscious. She shows him the immense scale of Madra.
characters.name: Star-like woman

characters.description: The world on which Jiran lives. During his interrupted Challenger transition, a star-like woman shows him Madra as an almost incomprehensibly immense globe attended by nine suns, revealing a scale far beyond what he had understood.
characters.name: Madra

characters.description: Jiran's named connection to the system-like force. She confirms that his family is alive, says Niya is safe but following a dangerous path, and urges him to investigate Madra's weakening through a node leading to the Jeweled Isles.
characters.name: Daughter

characters.description: A young combatant traveling with her cousin Cameron and a Tier 4 hunting party as the Graymin invasion worsens. She believes that finding an exceptionally capable boy could give the Empire a chance to survive, despite Cameron's skepticism.
characters.name: Olive

characters.description: Olive's cousin and a Tier 4 fighter whose abilities emphasize strength, durability, regeneration, and defense. He travels with her during the Graymin crisis but doubts that the Empire should rest its hopes on finding one remarkable boy.
characters.name: Cameron

characters.description: A dark-haired noble who joins Niya in searching his family fortress for a crystalline key. He confronts and kills his abusive stepfather, after which Niya keeps the key until their agreement is fulfilled.
characters.name: Dark-haired noble

characters.description: A pursuer seeking Jiran and a stolen crystalline key. When a shadow-wielding revolutionary leader tells him that the key's taker is connected to the blue-fire-and-lightning youth he wants, Markhiss agrees to trace her location.
characters.name: Markhiss

characters.description: A Tier 3 islander whose camouflage and ancestral traits lead Jiran to mistake her for a hostile scout. Their first encounter turns violent before a translation reward finally lets them understand each other.
characters.name: Mayalyn

characters.description: Mayalyn's uncle, the leader of Azure Light, and the community's greatest aura master. Mayalyn expects him to decide what will happen to Jiran after the outsider's arrival at the restricted metal rise.
characters.name: Amra

characters.description: Mayalyn's great-grandfather, remembered as the creator whose technological legacy she feels responsible for preserving.
characters.name: Maker

characters.description: Mayalyn's father and Amra's younger brother. While Jiran and Mayalyn consider the threat predicted by community legends, he confirms that his people can sense emotional qualities through another person's aura, including Jiran's feelings.
characters.name: Mayalyn's father

characters.description: Mayalyn's mother, who helps organize Azure Light's evacuation while alpha predators and the island's eruption make the town untenable. She supports Jiran's underground route and helps secure political agreement among the survivors.
characters.name: Mayalyn's mother

characters.description: Mayalyn's aunt and an elder among the evacuees. During the flight from Azure Light, she blames Jiran for the catastrophe, insults Mayalyn, and challenges his attempt to keep the endangered group united until everyone reaches safety.
characters.name: Viola

characters.description: The full identity of the young Imperial traveling with Cameron. Her acclamation has directed them south toward the Outlands, even after she dismissed the rest of their party and continued with only her cousin.
characters.name: Oliviala LeCruex

characters.description: A Tier 5 revolutionary collaborator working with Niya. He helps her train displaced recruits, presents their new strength as a weapon against those who uprooted them, and wants Niya's crystalline key for an operation involving a hidden temple secret.
characters.name: Revolutionary faction leader

recaps.ending: Jiran enters a new Challenger portal alone after hunting Tier 5 beasts and reaching 185 percent growth, leaving the nature and cost of his next trial unknown. Mayalyn brings Olive and Cameron into the cavern of Azure Light's displaced survivors, where she challenges the elders' exclusion and argues for cooperation with the Empire. Olive intends to advocate for the refugees and carefully control the spread of Jiran's density-claiming method, while Cameron is oath-bound to protect Mayalyn's people. Niya remains elsewhere with the crystalline key. She is training displaced recruits but refuses a revolutionary plan to sacrifice them as a diversion, and she intends to enter a temple operation within two days to seek Jiran and her own freedom. Markhiss is closing on her for an unknown purpose. Madra is still dying despite the restoration of one density absorber node. Daughter warned that an unidentified entity was tracking Jiran, and contact with her ended. The Graymin invasion continues, and neither Lenton nor Samris has reunited with Jiran.
recaps.in_short: After a Challenger portal separates Jiran from his mentors, he wins the Tier 2 series, advances to Tier 3, and returns to Madra after a year has passed. Seeking answers in the Jeweled Isles, he meets Mayalyn, trains under Amra, and learns that Azure Light expects him to die saving the community. Amra betrays them, but Jiran and Mayalyn restore a density absorber node. Its activation destroys the island, and they evacuate 341 of 345 residents. In the Outlands, Jiran prepares for another challenge while teaching Mayalyn, Olive, and Cameron new ways to control mana and claim density. The method could strengthen the Empire against the Graymin, but it could also destabilize the Church and its emperors. Jiran enters his next portal alone. Mayalyn, Olive, and Cameron approach the displaced community with an Imperial alliance, while Niya prepares a separate temple operation with the crystalline key as Markhiss closes in.

recaps.text: Previously: Jiran survived a failed tearing that damaged his aura and left his advancement far outside ordinary limits. He developed unusual methods for converting density into mana, gained an active second mind and a nascent mana body, and helped expose an illegal operation involving enslaved children. He also killed the people responsible. His actions drew the emperor's notice. Lenton became his instructor and protector, while the cursed noble Samris mentored him and Niya trained beside him. Jiran hopes to find a way to cure both mentors. His abnormal growth and attributes already exceed the usual Tier 2 limits, making his future politically dangerous as well as personally uncertain. At the opening of this volume, the group is in the Mushraha Desert. Samris must return to Feylon, while Jiran is expected to travel toward Scorata. Jiran remains bound to an approaching Challenger deadline that requires him to defeat a beast two tiers above himself, even as Lenton orders him to remain in camp and avoid further attention.

Jiran's work with Lenton's cube awakens his damaged mana body and an autonomous consciousness that helps process its senses. During a spar with Niya, he discovers that he can react to intended movements before they begin. He then uses elemental combinations to kill a large group of Tier 4 beasts, satisfying the apparent condition of his Challenger deadline. The resulting density instead opens a portal and drags him away, severing Lenton's fingers when the instructor tries to intervene. In a vast arena without ambient density, Jiran defeats successive metal opponents and places first in the Tier 2 Challenger series. A system failure holds him in stasis, after which an unnamed star-like woman appears, says Jiran created her through Revelation, and calls him her father. Jiran advances to Tier 3, physically ages from eight to fifteen, and awakens in a sealed forest enclosure. He refuses a new quest to restore a node in the Jeweled Isles, uses an ancient transference grid to return to the Finlist Empire, and reaches Solorin while searching for Niya, Lenton, Samris, and his family.

A year has passed outside Jiran's stasis. The Graymin have overrun several forts, and the Empire's defenders are being drawn away from their communities. Jiran learns to move deliberately with his mana body and develops aerial movement and gravity manipulation. A timed quest sends him to rescue fifteen civilians from a Tier 5 beast; eleven survive, and Jiran gains a map interface. Returning to a nearly deserted Feylon, he finds Samris devastated by his disappearance. Jiran's parents left for the Church of the Voice's central sanctuary, while Daughter says Niya is alive but following a dangerous course. Daughter also says Madra is weakening and urges him toward the Jeweled Isles. Samris departs alone after giving Jiran a ring that can summon him if a cure is found, together with a warning never to fight an Inquisitor. Jiran then accepts the island mission and crosses through a restored node. Elsewhere, Markhiss learns that the woman holding a stolen crystalline key is connected to the youth he has been seeking.

Jiran arrives on a tropical island with much greater ambient density than the Empire. He mistakes a camouflaged inhabitant for a Graymin scout and nearly kills her before a translation reward allows them to speak. The islander, Mayalyn, identifies him as an ungarnished outsider and fears the consequences of finding him near a sacred metal rise. After Jiran nearly kills himself protecting her from a giant predator, she leads him toward Azure Light and explains that her uncle Amra is the community's leader and greatest aura master. Four hunters attack the concealed outsider, but Jiran defeats them without killing anyone. Amra then arrives and suppresses him with overwhelming aura control. Once the dispute is contained, Jiran bargains for instruction: Amra will teach him, and Jiran will guide Amra and nine hunters to enough Tier 5 prey for them to advance. Mayalyn briefly believes the agreement also binds her to Jiran, but that misunderstanding is corrected. Jiran becomes Amra's disciple and receives access to a party interface.

Mayalyn privately concludes that Jiran matches a prophesied defender whose arrival signals the failure of Azure Light's protections and whose predecessors all died. She resolves to protect both him and the technological legacy of her great-grandfather, the Maker. Amra begins harsh aura training that forces Jiran to accept his present flaws and align his body, consciousness, and aura. Jiran ultimately expands his aura to an eleven-meter radius and learns that its shape is not inherently fixed. Exploring Azure Light, he finds Mayalyn exhausted from secret work in the Maker's underground laboratory. Together they revive a failing electrical device without using aura in the manner her people expected. The Maker's surviving research suggests that sufficiently advanced devices and observations are actively suppressed, and proposes that density itself may possess a combined sentience. Jiran also recognizes material connected to another world among the Maker's records, lending support to the old inventor's claims. The theory remains unproven, but it gives Jiran and Mayalyn a new explanation for Madra's technological limits.

Mayalyn and Jiran conclude that the inactive Makerdrives may be repairable, but Amra forbids the work and insists Jiran must fulfill the sacrificial role assigned to him. Jiran and Mayalyn become partners, and she finally tells him that Azure Light expects him to die stopping a future catastrophe. He rejects that fate and promises to seek a survivable alternative. Revelation confirms that Madra is sentient and wants Jiran's mana, though its edicts prevent a full explanation. Madra assigns him a mission to reactivate a density absorber node inside the island mountain. At the same time, Amra demands the promised expedition. After Jiran transports Amra and nine hunters to the Empire, Amra tries to hold him captive and replace Azure Light's old safeguards with ascended followers. Jiran escapes home and discovers that Mayalyn has been abducted and their repaired device destroyed. He follows the blood trail she deliberately left, forces her captors to release her, and learns that Madra is dying. Mayalyn is safe, but Amra's betrayal is now open and Jiran chooses to pursue the node.

Jiran enters the mountain alone and reaches the density absorber node through tunnels occupied by unfamiliar predators. There he perceives a vast reserve of Madra's mana inside his own soul. The node draws that power through his aura, nearly destroying him until he understands aura as an extension of his soul boundary and reinforces it. The mechanism restarts, but the activation triggers an eruption and island-wide catastrophe. Multiple alpha predators descend on Azure Light and overwhelm the Makerdrives. Mayalyn adapts the machines so Jiran can feed Madra's mana into them, buying time for 345 residents to flee through an underground route to the teleportation platform. Animated rock creatures attack during the final crossing, and Jiran destroys them with acid before escaping with a wounded hunter. The rescue records 341 survivors. Azure Light and its technology are lost. Jiran tells Mayalyn and her mother about Amra's coercion, then shares his hidden advancement history and connection to Madra with Mayalyn. She chooses to travel with him, monitor the effects of Challenger density, and leave before Amra returns.

With her parents' approval, Mayalyn leaves the displaced survivors and accompanies Jiran toward the Outlands. He begins hunting Tier 5 beasts to prepare for his next ascension while teaching her direct mana control. Each kill brings rapid growth, an extended Challenger timer, and a violent craving that Mayalyn monitors through his aura. She learns to claim mana manually and develops her elemental absorption abilities. When Jiran contacts Daughter for guidance about dangerous knowledge, he confronts her over the concealed consequences of restoring the node. Daughter admits using partial truths but says she is distinct from Madra and bound by Madra's rules. One restored node has made no measurable difference to the dying world, implying that many more may be needed. Daughter warns that Niya will soon require Jiran's help and that an unidentified entity is tracking him, then gives him a mission to win his next Challenger contest and extend the network of teleportation grids. Jiran and Mayalyn decide to move their camp, accelerate his preparations, investigate the emperors, and approach any future nodes together.

Oliviala LeCruex and Cameron reach Jiran's camp under the guidance of her acclamation, which she believes can lead to allies against the Graymin invasion. Cameron attacks Mayalyn by mistake, but Jiran stops him and the four establish a guarded alliance. Olive and Cameron then recognize Jiran as the boy who rescued them before his disappearance. During hunts, Mayalyn proves that she can store and release Jiran's elements with exceptional efficiency, while Cameron reaches the experience threshold for Tier 5. Olive formally binds Cameron to protect Mayalyn's people. Jiran learns that Olive is an emperor's daughter and Samris is an emperor's outcast son. He then teaches the cousins how a direct mental connection can control mana and claim density before it becomes growth. Both make rapid gains, but the discovery contradicts Church doctrine. Cameron explains that two church-aligned emperors have been unstable for centuries and could become uncontrollable beasts. Jiran's method could transform the war effort, yet careless disclosure might destabilize the Empire and provoke a catastrophe among its rulers.

Olive decides that Jiran's account of density may save the Empire, but also that its release must be tightly controlled. Revelation tells Jiran that Markhiss, likely a Tier 6 or Tier 7 Diviner, is hunting Niya for a purpose other than killing her and should reach her within five days. Mayalyn asks to present cooperation with the Empire directly to her displaced people. Jiran takes her, Olive, and Cameron to their cavern, where Mayalyn challenges the hunters enforcing the elders' ban and leads her Imperial allies inside. Olive intends to argue that remaining in the Empire is the refugees' best course, while Cameron's oath makes him their shield. Jiran hunts until he reaches 185 percent growth and a ninth concentration point. A new Challenger portal opens, locks his ascension, and he enters alone. Elsewhere, Niya teaches displaced recruits to claim density while retaining the crystalline key. She rejects a revolutionary plan to use the recruits as a diversion, but sets a two-day deadline for a temple operation because she believes its secret can lead her to Jiran and freedom. The book ends with both cousins moving toward separate dangers.
